name: Tabs
summary: A row (or column) of tabs that switches between panels of related content on the same page.
useWhen: Splitting one object into views of the same level (e.g. an entry's Content, SEO, Media, History).
Settings pages with a few sections, with --vertical.
Switching a view mode of the same data, with --filled (e.g. Grid / List).

dontUseWhen.case: Moving between pages of the app (the URL changes)
dontUseWhen.use: sidebar or navigation links with aria-current

dontUseWhen.case: Steps that must be done in order
Filtering a list by a value
More than about 7 sections, or content people need to compare side by side

anatomy.description: Optional wrapper around a scrolling .gds-tabs. Shows fade edges when the fade modifiers are set by JS.
The tab list. Horizontal with a bottom border by default; scrolls sideways when it overflows.

attributes.aria-label: What the tabs switch between, e.g. "Entry sections"

anatomy.description: One tab. A <button> (the CSS resets its button styles).

attributes.aria-selected: "true" on the active tab, "false" on the others
attributes.tabindex: 0 on the active tab, -1 on the others (arrow keys move focus)

anatomy.description: Leading icon slot. Holds a Lucide <i>. Decorative.
Tab label. Required unless the tab is --icon-only.
Slot for a small gds-badge (e.g. a count) after the label.
Red dot that means "something new". Add hidden text for screen readers next to it.
Close button for closable tabs (12px Lucide x). See known issues: a button inside a tab is a nested control.

modifiers.description: Segmented look: grey track, the active tab is a filled pill. Good for view switches.
Folder-tab look: the active tab joins the panel below.
Tabs in a column with a left indicator. Set the width (e.g. var(--tab-vertical-width)) and aria-orientation="vertical".
Smaller tabs and text. Without it tabs are the normal size.
The selected tab. Always with aria-selected="true".
Dimmed and blocks the mouse. Also set aria-disabled="true" (keyboard can still reach it).
Tab with only an icon, no gap. Needs aria-label on the tab.
Shows the left fade. Set by JS when the list is scrolled away from the start.
Shows the right fade. Set by JS when more tabs are hidden on the right.

states.name: selected
states.how: gds-tab--active + aria-selected="true" + tabindex="0"; its panel is visible, the other panels have the hidden attribute.

states.name: hover
states.how: Native :hover darkens the label and icon.

states.name: focus
states.how: Native :focus-visible: thicker indicator in the focus colour (bordered, vertical), inset outline (filled, card).

a11y: Use the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: role="tablist" on .gds-tabs, role="tab" on each .gds-tab, role="tabpanel" on each panel.
Each tab has aria-selected and aria-controls; each panel has an id and aria-labelledby pointing back at its tab, plus tabindex="0" when it has no focusable content.
Keyboard: Tab enters the list on the active tab; Left/Right (Up/Down when vertical) move between tabs; Home/End go to the first/last. The CSS does not do this; the product JS must.
Hide inactive panels with the hidden attribute so they are not read.
The status dot is colour only: add new next to it.

rules.rule: .gds-tabs has role="tablist" and every .gds-tab has role="tab".
rules.why: Without the roles, screen readers announce a row of unrelated buttons and the selected tab is not known.

rules.rule: Exactly one .gds-tab has gds-tab--active, and it is the only tab with aria-selected="true".
rules.why: The class draws the selection, the attribute announces it; they must agree.
rules.removeInV3: Style the active tab from [aria-selected="true"], so the class is not needed.

rules.rule: Every .gds-tab has aria-controls pointing to an element with role="tabpanel".
rules.why: Links each tab to the content it shows.

rules.rule: A gds-tab--icon-only tab has an aria-label.
rules.why: An icon alone has no accessible name.

rules.rule: Do not use tabs to link to other pages; use navigation with links and aria-current.
rules.why: Tabs switch content in place; pages change the URL and need real links.

rules.rule: A .gds-tabs has at most one of --filled and --card.
rules.why: The two looks override each other.

knownIssues.issue: The docs build tabs as <nav> with plain buttons: no role="tablist"/"tab", no aria-selected, no panels.
knownIssues.fix: Update all docs examples to the ARIA tabs pattern in this contract.

knownIssues.issue: The closable tab in the docs is a <div class="gds-tab"> with a button inside. As role="tab" this is a nested control, and the div is not focusable. .gds-tab__close also has no :focus-visible style.
knownIssues.fix: Support Delete to close on the focused tab and make the close button tabindex="-1", or move the close button outside the tab element; add a focus style to __close.

knownIssues.issue: --active and --disabled are classes only; nothing ties them to aria-selected / aria-disabled. --disabled uses pointer-events: none, so keyboard users can still activate it.
In --vertical the active tab text uses the hover colour (text-primary) while the other variants use action-primary.
knownIssues.fix: Confirm with design; if not intended, use --tab-color-active in vertical too.

knownIssues.issue: .gds-tabs-wrap and its fade modifiers are not shown in the docs and need JS that GDS does not ship.
knownIssues.fix: Add a docs example with the small scroll script, or remove the wrapper.

knownIssues.issue: --vertical combined with --filled or --card is not designed; the styles mix.
knownIssues.fix: Document as unsupported, or add a check.
